content.value_statement: Local roadmap data can drift from ClickUp work tracking. This skill guides MCP setup, sync commands, mapping rules, and conflict handling.
actual_capabilities: Maps local epics to ClickUp tasks marked as epics.
Maps local milestones to subtasks under their parent epic.
Documents status mappings from planned, in-progress, and done to ClickUp states.
Describes a local ClickUp configuration file for workspace, space, folder, and sync mappings.
Lists setup, push, pull, sync, status, link, and unlink commands.
Defines default conflict rules for status, points, and title fields.
limitations: Does not include executable sync scripts or a ClickUp API client.
Requires the official ClickUp MCP and OAuth authentication.
Assumes local roadmap data follows the documented epic and milestone model.
Does not describe custom conflict rules beyond the listed defaults.

use_cases.title: Keep Roadmaps Aligned
use_cases.description: Sync local planning epics and milestones with ClickUp so implementation status stays visible.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Review pull, push, and status workflows before updating team execution boards.

use_cases.title: Set Up ClickUp MCP
use_cases.description: Use the setup guidance to connect a workspace, space, and epic folder through OAuth.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure ClickUp roadmap synchronization for a workspace, space, and Epics folder. Explain each setup decision before changes are made.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Local Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my local roadmap with ClickUp and prepare a dry-run push plan. Highlight epics, milestones, and status changes.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Sync Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review sync conflicts between local roadmap data and ClickUp. Apply status from ClickUp, then keep local points and titles.

prompt_templates.title: Run Bidirectional Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe bidirectional sync workflow for my release roadmap. Include pull order, dry-run checks, manual links, and status verification.

output_examples.input: I need to connect a roadmap to ClickUp.
output_examples.output: Setup plan: choose the workspace, select the product space, confirm the Epics folder, then authenticate through ClickUp MCP.

output_examples.input: What will change if I push today?
output: Milestone user-auth M1 links under that epic.
No status updates until remote changes are pulled.

output_examples.output: Recommendation: keep the local title for planning consistency, but keep the ClickUp status because it reflects current delivery state.

best_practices: Pull from ClickUp before every push to reduce stale updates.
Use dry-run previews before changing ClickUp tasks.
Check sync status after link, unlink, or bidirectional sync operations.
anti_patterns: Pushing local changes before reviewing remote ClickUp updates.
Changing task links manually without recording the mapping.
Treating local status as authoritative when ClickUp reflects current work.

faq.question: Does this skill run ClickUp sync by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and command guidance. The actual sync depends on the ClickUp MCP and user-approved actions.

faq.question: Which ClickUp objects does it map?
faq.answer: It maps local epics to ClickUp tasks and local milestones to subtasks under the epic.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup notes use the official ClickUp MCP and ClickUp OAuth authentication.

faq.question: Can I preview changes first?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends dry-run previews before pushing updates to ClickUp.

faq.question: How are conflicts resolved?
faq.answer: ClickUp status wins because it shows current delivery. Local points and titles win because they represent planning data.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
